findings.title: Changing span keys from sets to sorted sets has no rollout compatibility path
findings.body: Existing live span-buffer keys are Redis Sets, created by the previous SADD/SUNIONSTORE implementation and retained for up to redis_ttl. After deploying this change, ZADD against any such key raises WRONGTYPE; the new Lua script also calls ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on those keys and will fail. During a rolling deployment, old workers likewise cannot SADD to keys created by new workers. This can make span processing fail for active traces until the old keys expire, with no migration, key versioning, or coordinated drain included.

findings.title: The optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime values
findings.body: This branch passes order_by="-datetime" to OptimizedCursorPaginator, but that paginator computes cursor keys with math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so building the first cursor for any non-empty result page raises TypeError and returns a 500 to authorized users requesting optimized_pagination=true. The paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime serialization/deserialization, or this endpoint must continue using DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE makes replayed span scores non-idempotent
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE uses SUM as its default aggregate. A normally expected Kafka replay can put the same payload in both set_key and the temporary parent/span key: for example, replaying a child after its parent redirect has already moved that child into the destination. The union then doubles end_timestamp_precise for that member, and repeated replays continue increasing it. Since ZPOPMIN uses this score for eviction, replayed spans are incorrectly protected while newer valid spans are evicted. Use an explicit aggregate such as MAX (or otherwise preserve the existing member score) when merging.

findings.title: Eviction ignores the configured max_segment_spans limit
findings.body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the prior enforcement was removed from _load_segment_data and the Lua script now unconditionally caps every segment at 1000. Callers configured with a lower limit can now flush up to 1000 spans despite their memory/safety setting, while callers configured with a higher limit silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit as a script argument and use it for eviction.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause invalid Django queryset slices
findings.body: The advertised advanced path passes a negative start_offset directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexing/slice bounds with ValueError rather than interpreting them as reverse pagination. Thus an authorized client supplying a negative cursor offset receives a 500, not the documented bidirectional pagination behavior. Negative offsets need to be translated into a supported cursor query or rejected during cursor validation.

findings.title: Reducing redirect traversal fragments deeply nested traces
findings.body: The redirect walk was reduced from 10,000 iterations to 1,000 without another mechanism to collapse old redirect chains. For a trace whose parent chain exceeds roughly 1,000 links, a later child resolves only to an intermediate span buffer and is recorded there instead of the root buffer, producing separate incomplete segments. The 1,000-member payload eviction limit does not bound redirect-chain depth, because redirect mappings remain after payload eviction. Preserve the previous traversal bound or add path compression/a defined depth handling strategy.
